subject: Next steps: Evaluation criteria & model selection for NovaCorp POC
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novacorp.com>; Marcus Reed <m.reed@novacorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed success criteria for NovaCorp POC

Lena / Marcus — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the POC planning.

Call summary (5 min):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for NovaCorp's customer-facing summarization and multilingual search features.
- Key constraints: latency < 250ms 95th, support for en/es/pt, no customer data persisted outside VPC during trial.
- Stakeholders: Lena (product), Marcus (ML), Procurement (contract).

Proposed POC scope & success criteria (actionable):
1) Quality: model produces summaries with ROUGE-L >= 0.55 vs NovaCorp golden set (bench of 200 docs) and human acceptance >= 85% on Key UX checks.
2) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end latency < 250ms at 10 RPS simulated workload.
3) Multilingual coverage: support for English, Spanish, Portuguese with language-specific prompt templates and fallback quality degradation < 10%.
4) Cost baseline: tokens/unit cost target to be agreed — initial budget cap $6k for 2-week trial.
5) Operational: streaming enabled, canaries for model fallback, and logs to your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch.

Model recommendation for trial (initial pick):
- Primary: Open-Llama-3-13B-int8 (latency/quality balance for summarization).
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B-quant (favored for lower memory footprint and stable inferencing on our dedicated pool).
- Note: we can run small compare set with an instruction-tuned multilang variant if you want stronger Spanish/Portuguese baselines.

Immediate next steps (owners + timeline):
- Redwood to provide: POC plan doc, test set ingestion guide, and model matrix by EOD Thurs (May 21). (Owner: Sean)
- NovaCorp to provide: golden evaluation set (200 docs), target latency profile, and security checklist for Private deployment option by Mon, May 25. (Owner: Lena)
- Procurement to confirm NDA/SOW template and expected contracting timeline by May 28. (Owner: procurement@novacorp.com)

Attachments: novacorp_poc_scope.pdf (scope draft), redwood_model_matrix.xlsx (initial model tradeoffs).

I’ll follow up with the POC doc and a simple HubSpot milestone created for tracking. If any of the success criteria above look off, please tell me what to change.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0114

---
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novacorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Reed <m.reed@novacorp.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, procurement@novacorp.com
Date: 2026-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed success criteria for NovaCorp POC

Thanks Sean — this is exactly the level of clarity we needed. A couple quick clarifications/questions from our side: 

1) Golden set composition: the 200 docs — could we break that into 120 English / 50 Spanish / 30 Portuguese? That aligns with our production distribution.
2) Latency: is the 10 RPS simulated at average document length 500 tokens? We can adjust but want to be explicit.
3) Model selection: Marcus is worried that Open-Llama-3 may underperform on Portuguese. Would you be open to running a three-way compare (Open-Llama-3, Llama-2-13B-quant, and a smaller instruction-tuned multilingual model) in the first 2 days of the trial?
4) Security: we will share a redacted sample and a SOC2 questionnaire; we prefer Private deployment but can start hosted if the security answers are quick.

Procurement — looping you in; can you confirm whether NovaCorp needs a PO before a two-week eval or if an MSA + SOW will suffice?

Appreciate it — aiming to kick off testing week of June 1.

Best,
Lena
Head of Product, NovaCorp
Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novacorp.com>

---
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novacorp.com>, Marcus Reed <m.reed@novacorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, procurement@novacorp.com
Date: 2026-05-20T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed success criteria for NovaCorp POC

Lena — great points; quick answers and updated plan inline.

1) Golden set composition: absolutely — updated plan will call out 120/50/30 split. That helps us weight scoring per language.
2) Latency workload: yes, baseline assumed avg 500 tokens per request; we’ll include a sensitivity run at 250/500/1,000 tokens.
3) Model compare: happy to run a three-way compare in Days 0–2. Proposed small comparison set (50 examples across languages) to pick the best primary model for Days 3–14. The three models we’ll compare: Open-Llama-3-13B-int8, Llama-2-13B-quant, and Mistral-7B-instruct (multilingual-tuned).
   - Success rule for picking primary: relative quality delta < 5% means choose the lowest-cost model; otherwise pick the higher-quality model.
4) Security/deployment: we can support Private deployment for the POC; to keep timeline, we can do a hybrid: Hosted for the three-way compare, switch to Private for the full run once SOC2 answers are confirmed.

Updated owners & timeline (short):
- Fri May 21 EOD: Redwood to share updated POC doc with language split, test harness, and model compare plan. (Sean)
- Mon May 25: NovaCorp uploads golden set and SOC2 responses. (Lena)
- Tue May 26: Redwood spins up hosted test endpoints and runs three-way compare with sample set; share interim results by EOD. (Sean / Monica)
- Week of June 1: Full 2-week run with chosen primary model; monitoring and regular syncs.

Attachments: attached small_test_instructions.txt (inline stub) — real test harness will be shared in Drive link.

Let me know if Procurement needs any templated SOW language; we have a short eval SOW we can push into your template to speed approvals.

Thanks,
Sean
---
From: procurement@novacorp.com
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novacorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed success criteria for NovaCorp POC

Hi Sean — procurement here. We typically need an MSA in place and a short eval SOW rather than a PO for trials under $25k. Please send your standard eval SOW and confirm Redwood’s billing contact and invoicing address. Also include whether there are any data transfer or hosting costs we should expect if NovaCorp chooses Private deployment after the trial.

If you can get the SOW and billing details to me today, we can keep to the kickoff week of June 1.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
NovaCorp
procurement@novacorp.com
